subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated in October 1958 by:
explanation: Iskander Mirza abrogated the constitution and declared martial law on 7 October 1958; Ayub Khan ousted him weeks later.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 1962 Constitution was abrogated in March 1969 by:
explanation: When Ayub Khan resigned, he handed power to army chief Yahya Khan, who abrogated the constitution and imposed martial law.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Twelfth Amendment (1991) provided for:
o: The creation of the Federal Shariat Court
Speedy trial courts for heinous offences
explanation: Passed under Nawaz Sharif's first government, the 12th Amendment set up speedy trial courts for a limited period to deal with serious crimes.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Zia-ul-Haq's Provisional Constitution Order of 1981 required judges of the superior courts to:
o: Take a fresh oath under the Order
explanation: The PCO curtailed the courts' powers and required a new oath; several judges who refused were removed.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The First Amendment to the 1973 Constitution (1974) was related to:
o: Redefining Pakistan's territories after the recognition of Bangladesh
explanation: The First Amendment removed references to East Pakistan after Pakistan recognised Bangladesh in 1974.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Second Amendment to the Constitution (1974):
explanation: Passed in September 1974 under Bhutto, the Second Amendment defined a non-Muslim to include the Ahmadis.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Article 58(2)(b), inserted by the Eighth Amendment, empowered the President to:
o: Appoint the Chief Justice without consultation
Dissolve the National Assembly at his discretion
explanation: Article 58(2)(b) let the President dismiss governments and dissolve the Assembly, making him far stronger than the Prime Minister.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Eighth Amendment (1985) is known mainly for:
o: Indemnifying martial law actions and shifting power towards the President
explanation: Passed by the Junejo-era Parliament, it validated Zia's martial law measures and gave the President sweeping powers.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Zia-ul-Haq revived the 1973 Constitution with major changes through the:
o: Revival of the Constitution of 1973 Order, 1985
explanation: The 1985 Revival of the Constitution Order restored the suspended constitution with amendments strengthening the President; the Eighth Amendment later validated it.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Thirteenth Amendment (1997) is known for:
o: Removing the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly
explanation: Nawaz Sharif's government used its heavy majority to delete Article 58(2)(b) through the 13th Amendment.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which amendment restored the President's power under Article 58(2)(b) in 2003?
explanation: The 17th Amendment, agreed with the MMA under Musharraf, revived the dissolution power subject to Supreme Court review.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Seventeenth Amendment (2003) largely gave constitutional cover to:
explanation: The 17th Amendment incorporated most of Musharraf's Legal Framework Order into the Constitution.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Article 58(2)(b) was finally omitted from the Constitution by the:
explanation: The 18th Amendment of 2010 removed the President's discretionary dissolution power, restoring the parliamentary character of the Constitution.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which amendment abolished the Concurrent Legislative List and devolved many subjects to the provinces?
explanation: The 18th Amendment deleted the Concurrent List, so subjects such as education and health passed largely to the provinces.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The North-West Frontier Province was renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by the:
explanation: The 18th Amendment of April 2010 changed the name of NWFP to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which restriction, added under Musharraf, was removed by the 18th Amendment?
o: The requirement that the President be a Muslim
The bar on a person becoming Prime Minister a third time
explanation: The 18th Amendment removed the bar on third terms, which allowed Nawaz Sharif to become Prime Minister again in 2013.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Article 175-A, inserted by the 18th Amendment, created:
o: The Judicial Commission of Pakistan for appointing superior court judges
explanation: The 18th Amendment replaced the old consultative method with a Judicial Commission and a parliamentary committee for appointments to the superior courts.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Parliamentary Committee on Constitutional Reform, which drafted the 18th Amendment, was chaired by:
explanation: Senator Mian Raza Rabbani led the all-party committee whose consensus draft became the 18th Amendment.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Nineteenth Amendment (2011) mainly revised:
o: The procedure for appointing superior court judges
explanation: After the Supreme Court raised concerns about the 18th Amendment's appointment process, the 19th Amendment enlarged the Judicial Commission and changed the committee's role.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Twentieth Amendment (2012) is known for providing:
o: A consensual mechanism for appointing caretaker governments
Constitutional benches in the Supreme Court
explanation: The 20th Amendment required caretaker Prime Ministers and Chief Ministers to be chosen through consultation between government and opposition.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which constitutional amendment created military courts in Pakistan?
explanation: The 21st Amendment of January 2015 provided for military courts to try terrorism suspects for two years.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 21st Amendment was passed in January 2015 in response to:
o: The attack on the Army Public School, Peshawar
explanation: After the December 2014 massacre at the Army Public School, Parliament passed the 21st Amendment as part of the National Action Plan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 23rd Amendment (2017):
o: Extended military courts for a further two years
Changed the tenure of the Chief Justice
explanation: When the 21st Amendment's two-year sunset expired, the 23rd Amendment revived military courts until 2019.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 24th Amendment (2017) allowed:
o: The merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Delimitation of constituencies on the basis of the provisional 2017 census
The creation of the Islamabad High Court
explanation: To hold the 2018 elections on time, the 24th Amendment let seats be allocated using the provisional results of the 2017 census.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: FATA was merged with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under which amendment to the Constitution?
explanation: The 25th Amendment of May 2018 abolished FATA's separate status and merged the tribal areas into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under the 26th Amendment (2024), the Chief Justice of Pakistan is nominated by:
o: A Special Parliamentary Committee from among the three most senior judges
The Judicial Commission from among all Supreme Court judges
explanation: The 26th Amendment ended automatic seniority; a parliamentary committee now nominates the Chief Justice from the three senior-most judges for a three-year term.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 26th Amendment (2024) provided for:
o: Constitutional benches in the Supreme Court and High Courts
explanation: The amendment created constitutional benches to hear constitutional petitions and matters of public importance.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 27th Amendment (2025) established:
explanation: The 27th Amendment created a Federal Constitutional Court to decide constitutional disputes, to hear constitutional matters separately from the Supreme Court.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first capital of Pakistan was:
explanation: Karachi served as the federal capital from 1947 until the government moved to Rawalpindi and then Islamabad under Ayub Khan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah died on:
explanation: The Quaid died in Karachi on 11 September 1948, barely thirteen months after independence.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who succeeded Quaid-i-Azam as Governor-General of Pakistan?
explanation: Khawaja Nazimuddin, Chief Minister of East Bengal, became Governor-General after the Quaid's death in 1948.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first President of Pakistan's Constituent Assembly was:
explanation: Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947, besides being Governor-General; Jogendra Nath Mandal chaired the opening session.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan's first Law Minister was:
explanation: Jogendra Nath Mandal, a Scheduled Caste leader from Bengal, held the law and labour portfolio in Liaquat's first cabinet.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: At Dhaka in March 1948, Quaid-i-Azam declared that the state language of Pakistan would be:
explanation: Jinnah's declaration in favour of Urdu alone was resented by Bengali students and became a starting point of the Language Movement.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Bengali Language Movement's martyrs of 21 February 1952 are commemorated worldwide as:
explanation: UNESCO declared 21 February International Mother Language Day in memory of the students killed in Dhaka in 1952.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated in 1951 at:
explanation: Liaquat was shot while addressing a public meeting at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi, later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who was the second Prime Minister of Pakistan?
explanation: After Liaquat's assassination in 1951, Khawaja Nazimuddin stepped down as Governor-General to become Prime Minister.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Governor-General dismissed Prime Minister Khawaja Nazimuddin in 1953, even though he had a majority in the Assembly?
explanation: Ghulam Muhammad's dismissal of Nazimuddin in April 1953 began the pattern of executive interference with elected governments.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who succeeded Khawaja Nazimuddin as Prime Minister in 1953?
explanation: Ghulam Muhammad recalled Muhammad Ali Bogra, then ambassador to the United States, to head the government.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Rawalpindi Conspiracy of 1951, an attempted coup, was led by:
explanation: Major General Akbar Khan and a group of officers and leftist intellectuals, including Faiz Ahmed Faiz, were tried for plotting to overthrow the government.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan's first, localised martial law was imposed in 1953 in:
explanation: Martial law was declared in Lahore in March 1953 to control the anti-Ahmadiyya disturbances.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the East Bengal provincial elections of 1954, the Muslim League was routed by the:
explanation: The United Front of Fazlul Haq, Suhrawardy and Maulana Bhashani won an overwhelming majority, reducing the League to a handful of seats.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The One Unit scheme of 1955:
o: Merged the provinces and states of West Pakistan into a single province
United East and West Pakistan under one legislature
explanation: One Unit amalgamated Punjab, Sindh, NWFP, Balochistan and the princely states into West Pakistan to balance East Pakistan under parity.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: One Unit was dissolved in 1970 by:
explanation: Yahya Khan restored the four provinces of West Pakistan on 1 July 1970 before the general elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Prime Minister of the 1950s led the Awami League?
explanation: Suhrawardy headed an Awami League–Republican coalition government in 1956–57.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Prime Minister of Pakistan held office for only about two months in 1957?
explanation: I. I. Chundrigar's government lasted from October to December 1957, reflecting the instability of the period.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Gwadar became part of Pakistan in 1958 during the premiership of:
explanation: Feroz Khan Noon's government acquired Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: How many Prime Ministers did Pakistan have from 1947 until the martial law of October 1958?
explanation: Liaquat, Nazimuddin, Bogra, Chaudhry Muhammad Ali, Suhrawardy, Chundrigar and Noon held office, showing the instability of the parliamentary period.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The last Governor-General of Pakistan was:
explanation: Iskander Mirza became Governor-General in 1955 and, under the 1956 Constitution, the first President.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who became Pakistan's first President under the 1956 Constitution?
explanation: Iskander Mirza, the last Governor-General, took office as President when the 1956 Constitution came into force.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Liaquat-Nehru Pact of 1950 dealt mainly with:
o: The protection of minorities in both countries
explanation: Signed in Delhi in April 1950 after communal violence in Bengal, the pact committed both governments to protect their minorities.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Khan of Kalat signed the instrument of accession to Pakistan in:
explanation: The Khan of Kalat, Mir Ahmad Yar Khan, acceded to Pakistan in March 1948.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who was the first woman to be appointed Governor of a province in Pakistan?
explanation: Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan, widow of the first Prime Minister, served as Governor of Sindh from 1973 to 1976.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan's first nationwide martial law was proclaimed on 7 October 1958 by:
explanation: Iskander Mirza abrogated the constitution and appointed Ayub Khan Chief Martial Law Administrator; Ayub removed Mirza within three weeks.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The system of Basic Democracies was introduced in 1959 by:
explanation: Ayub's Basic Democracies created tiers of local councils whose members also served as the electoral college.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Ayub Khan's Elective Bodies Disqualification Order (EBDO) of 1959 was used to:
o: Bar many politicians from public life
explanation: Under EBDO, politicians accused of misconduct could be disqualified from elective office, removing many opponents of the regime.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The West Pakistan Land Reforms Regulation was issued in:
explanation: Ayub's land reforms of 1959 set ceilings on individual landholdings; further reforms followed under Bhutto in 1972.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance was promulgated in:
explanation: Ayub Khan's 1961 Ordinance regulated marriage, divorce, polygamy and inheritance by orphaned grandchildren.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under Ayub Khan, the federal capital was shifted from Karachi to:
explanation: Ayub's government decided to build a new capital, Islamabad, near Rawalpindi, which served as the interim capital.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: During the Ayub era, a contested presidential election was held in:
explanation: In January 1965 Ayub Khan defeated Fatima Jinnah in an indirect election through the Basic Democrats.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the presidential election of 1965, Ayub Khan was opposed by:
explanation: The Combined Opposition Parties chose Fatima Jinnah as their candidate; she lost in the Basic Democrats' vote.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Pakistan Peoples Party was founded in 1967 at:
explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto founded the PPP at a convention in Lahore after leaving Ayub's government over the Tashkent Declaration.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman presented his Six Points in:
explanation: Mujib announced the Six Points at Lahore in 1966, demanding wide autonomy for East Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sheikh Mujib's Six Points demanded:
o: A loose federation leaving defence and foreign affairs with the centre
Restoration of parity between the wings
A presidential system elected by Basic Democrats
explanation: The Six Points would have left only defence and foreign affairs to the centre and given the provinces control over taxation, currency and trade.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Agartala Conspiracy Case (1968) was brought against:
explanation: Mujib and others were accused of conspiring with India; the case made him a hero in East Pakistan and was withdrawn in 1969.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who became President after Ayub Khan resigned?
explanation: Ayub handed power to army chief Yahya Khan, who imposed martial law and became President.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Ayub Khan was first confirmed as President through a vote of the Basic Democrats in a referendum held in:
explanation: In February 1960 the newly elected Basic Democrats voted confidence in Ayub Khan, who then took oath as President.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After being ousted in October 1958, Iskander Mirza spent the rest of his life in exile in:
explanation: Ayub Khan sent Mirza abroad; he lived in London until his death in 1969 and was buried in Tehran.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan's first general elections held directly on the basis of adult franchise took place in:
explanation: The December 1970 elections were the first nationwide direct elections on adult franchise.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the 1970 elections, the party that won the most seats in West Pakistan was the:
explanation: Bhutto's PPP won a majority of West Pakistan's seats, while the Awami League swept East Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Awami League's result in the 1970 elections was significant because:
o: It won seats in every province of West Pakistan
It won an absolute majority in the National Assembly entirely from East Pakistan
It formed a coalition government with the PPP
explanation: Winning 160 of East Pakistan's 162 general seats gave the Awami League a majority in the 300-member Assembly without a single seat in the West.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The military operation launched in East Pakistan on 25 March 1971 was code-named:
explanation: After talks failed, the army began Operation Searchlight in Dhaka, which led to civil war in East Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Dhaka fell and East Pakistan separated on:
explanation: Pakistani forces in the east surrendered at Dhaka on 16 December 1971, and Bangladesh emerged as an independent state.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The commission that inquired into the causes of the 1971 debacle was headed by:
explanation: Chief Justice Hamoodur Rahman's commission examined the political and military failures that led to the loss of East Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who is the only person to have held the office of Vice-President of Pakistan?
explanation: Nurul Amin, one of the two non-Awami League members elected from East Pakistan in 1970, was made Vice-President in December 1971.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan's only civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator was:
explanation: Bhutto took over from Yahya Khan in December 1971 as President and Chief Martial Law Administrator.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who became President of Pakistan when the 1973 Constitution came into force?
explanation: Bhutto became Prime Minister under the new parliamentary constitution, and Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry was elected President.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The State of Swat was merged into Pakistan in:
explanation: Swat, Dir and Chitral lost their status as princely states in 1969 and were merged into Pakistan as districts.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In 1973, the federal government dismissed the NAP–JUI provincial government of Balochistan headed by:
explanation: Bhutto's government removed Chief Minister Ataullah Mengal in February 1973, which led to an insurgency and military operation in Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Bhutto's government banned the National Awami Party in 1975 after the assassination of:
explanation: After PPP leader Hayat Sherpao was killed in a bomb blast in Peshawar in 1975, the NAP was banned and its leaders tried before the Hyderabad Tribunal.
